**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, confidence 0.95)**

**Clause:** § 2.2 (p0013) — "Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term."

**Why it fails:** This is a sole-supplier obligation binding *us*, running for the full three-year term (§ 8.1), with no product-category limitation and no performance-based exit. That is squarely in walk-away territory and misses the fallback (defined category + 12 months + automatic termination on SLA/delivery failure) on every material term.

**Internal conflict noted:** § 2.1 states "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies," and § 12.3 has Vendor acknowledge that "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." Section 2.2 contradicts both, so deletion is the cleanest fix and restores consistency rather than merely trimming the clause.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** delete p0013 in full, with a comment offering the category-limited, 12-month, SLA-terminable fallback if Silverline needs some protection.

Exclusivity or non-exclusivity running in our favour was checked and left alone (e.g., the non-exclusive access licence in § 13.1, exclusive jurisdiction in § 28.2, and exclusive-remedy references in §§ 19.4, 21.4, 30.2 are unrelated to this rule).
